messages.text: 1. Changes in market conditions Staking returns depend directly on current network and economic indicators: token inflation, the amount of rewards in the blockchain, validator activity, and the total number of coins participating in staking.  2. Dynamic distribution of rewards in the network Many networks use mechanisms whereby the size of rewards is adjusted automatically. If more users connect to staking, the reward is distributed among a larger number of participants, so the percentage may decrease. 3. Features of a specific pool or validator Different pools or validators may have different fees, levels of efficiency, and amounts of delegated funds. All of this affects the actual percentage of return that the user receives. 4. Protocol changes and network updates Blockchain teams periodically make changes to the rules for calculating rewards. After such updates, yield indicators may change temporarily. 5. Internal platform mechanics If the platform uses a flexible yield model (e.g., floating APY), the percentage may be adjusted automatically based on market conditions, available liquidity pools, or asset allocation strategies.
